title: Maximal chains in a finite length module have length the length of the module and simple quotients
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite length module M and any maximal chain of submodules, the number of steps is the length of M, each successive quotient is simple of the form R modulo a maximal ideal, and the number of steps with a given maximal ideal equals the length of the localisation of M at it (statement lines 12762-12783). The proof does not compute with composition series abstractly: it first observes that a non-simple quotient would allow a refinement, then turns each simple quotient into a residue field, and finally localises at a single maximal ideal to isolate the steps belonging to it (proof lines 12785-12817). Locating the counting statement in the localised length is the step that carries the last part. H2.
